clue.text: Irish member vets bogus oath (spoken in 1720, perhaps)

indicators.note: something bogus is not genuine, so these letters are faked into a new order

explanation.surface: An Irish politician checks a fake pledge, as if spoken in a pirate's day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bogus' rearranges all fifteen letters of IRISH MEMBER VETS. The year 1720 points to the golden age of piracy, the theme of this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock exclamation of surprise put in the mouths of pirates, here a swearing phrase from that era.

clue.text: Old sailing ships vex Times

parts.note: to gall is to irritate or vex
eons are very long times or ages

explanation.surface: Old sailing ships causing trouble for people in times past.
explanation.definitionFit: Large square-rigged sailing vessels of the Spanish treasure fleets are the classic example.

clue.text: A river protects British on the defensive

indicators.note: the river's letters surround and shield the abbreviation for British

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

explanation.surface: A river serves as a defence for Britain, keeping invaders back.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being cornered and forced to fight back, as a hunted animal is.

clue.text: Old queen makes love among ship's timbers

indicators.note: the letter for love sits among the letters of the ship's timbers

parts.note: a carline is a fore-and-aft timber in a ship's deck framing
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A former queen has a romantic encounter down among a ship's timbers.
explanation.walkthrough: CARLINE (also carling) is a nautical word for a short timber running between deck beams.
explanation.definitionFit: Caroline of Ansbach and Caroline of Brunswick were both queen consorts of Britain.

clue.text: Notice small boarding party? Makes sense

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: the small letter boards, climbing into, the party's letters

parts.note: the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

explanation.surface: Spotting a small group boarding a ship turns out to be logical.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something that adds up is consistent and believable, as a correct sum is.

clue.text: I'd say young US man is able to pick up a Corsair

indicators.note: a phrase about speaking signals that the words are judged by their sound

parts.words: young US man is able to pick up
parts.note: a buck is a young man in American slang, is able to is can, and to pick up a sound is to hear

explanation.surface: A young American can catch a glimpse of a pirate ship on the horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, BUCK CAN HEAR comes out as the pirate's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsairs were pirates or privateers of the Barbary coast, so a synonym for a sea robber.

clue.text: Airline carries 16oz duck and port

indicators.note: the airline's letters carry the weight inside them

parts.note: BA is British Airways
sixteen ounces make one pound, written 1 LB with the 1 as I
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An airline flies a pound of duck to a seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilbao is a major seaport in the Basque Country of northern Spain.

clue.text: Support wet crewman controlling aid

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a cue or an arm
raining describes wet weather
a hand is a member of a ship's crew

explanation.surface: A sailor gets some support in wet weather from a shipmate.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone offering a curbing influence lends one, a guiding check on another's actions.

clue.text: Catch tense boy touring Norway (central region)

parts.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: the boy's letters travel round the letter for Norway

parts.note: a lad is a boy
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A youngster on a tour of Norway's interior hears something.
explanation.definitionFit: The core, central part of a country or territory, away from coasts and borders.

clue.text: Wee one blocks vessel close to shore

indicators.note: the numeral for one is wedged into the vessel's letters, blocking it

parts.note: an urn is a vessel
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A small object obstructs a boat near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wee' looks like Scottish 'small', but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wee is the colloquial word for what the bladder passes, so a direct synonym.

clue.text: Oval cone not completely reshaped?

indicators.note: letters reshaped are given a new form, a new order
the word cone is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A cone shape distorted into an oval, only partly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not completely' drops the last letter of CONE, and 'reshaped' mixes OVAL with CON. The whole clue also describes a mountain whose cone has been blown into a new shape.
explanation.definitionFit: An erupting mountain is a cone whose top is blasted away and remodelled, as the whole clue says.

clue.text: Old instrument still in position after fire

indicators.note: the word for still is placed after the word for fire

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
but means still, yet, nevertheless

explanation.surface: An antique instrument stays put after a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: An early form of trombone used in Renaissance and Baroque music.

clue.text: Man on board, occupant of crow's-nest?

definitions.meaning: a chess piece, a man on the chessboard, also called a castle
a bird of the crow family that nests in rookeries, taking the ship's lookout post literally

explanation.surface: A sailor aboard ship is the lookout up in the crow's-nest.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both a chess piece and a gregarious black bird of the crow family.

clue.text: 20 Polish in a rocky area

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A Polish person in a stony region.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 refers to the answer at 20-down, an island. It is also the name of the ship in Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean landmass shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic, an example of the 20-down answer.

clue.text: Hesitate limiting English prisoner's energy source

indicators.note: the hesitation word bounds the other letters, holding them in

parts.note: to waver is to hesitate
a POW is a prisoner of war

explanation.surface: Hesitation restricts an English prisoner's supply of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity generated from the motion of the sea's surface, a renewable source of power.

clue.text: Force to work in small space to free about 50

parts.note: an en is a small printer's space, half an em

indicators.note: the word for free goes about, around, the numeral

parts.note: to save is to rescue or free
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: Making people labour in a cramped space to release around fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone a slave is to compel them to labour without pay or freedom.

clue.text: He avoids the motive for crime

indicators.note: the word He is avoided, left out of the phrase

parts.note: the reason is the motive behind something

explanation.surface: A suspect dodges questions about why the crime was committed.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is a grave crime in law.

clue.text: Team leader to cheer up, having lost second prize

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the word for cheer up loses one letter for second

parts.note: to reassure is to cheer up or encourage

explanation.surface: A captain encourages the team after a runner-up finish.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to value highly or cherish, a synonym of prize in that sense.

clue.text: Perhaps divers sidebars need editing

indicators.note: text that needs editing will be rearranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Some magazine side-panels, maybe about divers, need revising.
explanation.walkthrough: Divers here are diving ducks and loons, not people in wetsuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers are a family of fish-eating water birds of coasts and open water, given as an example.

clue.text: Current point estimated to have moved around

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a tine is a point or prong, as of a fork
rated means estimated or valued

explanation.surface: An electric current at one point was estimated to have shifted.
explanation.definitionFit: To itinerate is to travel from place to place, as a circuit preacher does.

clue.text: One's left with kitchen unit

parts.note: I is one, so one's is I'S
and means with, together with

explanation.surface: Someone is left holding a cupboard after the kitchen refit.
explanation.definitionFit: A freestanding worktop block in the middle of a kitchen goes by this name.

clue.text: A doctor provided time off course

parts.note: if means provided, on condition that

explanation.surface: A doctor is granted a period away from his studies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off course' suggests a student taking a break, but means drifting from a route.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat floating loose without moorings or steering has wandered from its intended route.

clue.text: Principal sea area off Ireland, not large

indicators.note: not with the abbreviation for large means it is taken out

parts.note: Malin is a shipping forecast area off the north coast of Ireland
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: The chief sea zone off Ireland is not a big one.
explanation.walkthrough: The BBC shipping forecast divides British waters into named sea areas; Malin lies off Donegal.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means chief or most important, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Goldsmith holds papers up in port

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the name holds the papers inside it

parts.note: Zac Goldsmith is a British politician
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A goldsmith keeps his documents in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goldsmith' looks like a jeweller but is Zac Goldsmith, a British Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadiz is an ancient seaport on the Atlantic coast of southwestern Spain.

clue.text: Labour fails to suppress female PM

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold down the letter for female inside them
a party that fails falls apart, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Labour Party fails to silence a woman Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Balfour was Conservative Prime Minister of the UK from 1902 to 1905.

clue.text: Bridge is beginning to hinder one means of communication

parts.note: a span is a bridge or its arch

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bridge begins to obstruct a route between places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means of communication' suggests a road or link, but here it is a language.
explanation.definitionFit: A language is a means of communication, and this is one of the world's most widely spoken.

clue.text: Top fruit variety

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the head, so the first letter of the fruit goes

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: The best fruit of its kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as an adjective meaning best, but it is a verb meaning to behead.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of goods is an assortment or variety of them.

clue.text: Foreign Office ordered to tackle Republican taboo

indicators.note: the outer letters take on the abbreviation for Republican, grappling it between them

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the British Foreign Office
bidden means ordered or commanded

explanation.surface: The Foreign Office is told to take on a Republican over an off-limits topic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taboo is prohibited by custom, so not allowed.
